title: Scalable Passive QRAM
abstract: We present a blueprint for implementing the physical QRAM operation in a scalable, passive manner, proving its feasibility in principle. Our construction is passive because for an $n$-qubit address over $N = 2^n$ memory bits the energy cost per QRAM query is $O(\log N)$, and to our knowledge it is the first construction to use $\operatorname{polylog} N$ energy. The runtime for each query is $O(\log^2 N)$. It is achieved by evolving a pre-manufactured time-independent 4-local Hamiltonian with $O(N)$ terms where every qubit participates in at most 4 terms.

bite.hook: First QRAM construction to use polylogarithmic energy, costing O(log N) per query for N memory bits.
tldr: Designed a blueprint for implementing the physical QRAM operation in a scalable and passive manner.
Achieved the construction by evolving a pre-manufactured time-independent 4-local Hamiltonian with O(N) terms.
Proved feasibility in principle, achieving O(log N) energy cost per query and O(log^2 N) runtime.
bite.whyItMatters: Quantum Random Access Memory is a bottleneck for many quantum algorithms; making it energy-efficient is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to find one specific book in a giant library without turning on the lights at every shelf. This new blueprint figures out a clever, energy-efficient way to grab the right piece of quantum memory while wasting very little power.
